source.title: Predicting Grokking Long Before it Happens: A look into the loss landscape of models which grok
source.citation: Pascal Junior Tikeng Notsawo et al., 2023
source.authors: Pascal Junior Tikeng Notsawo; Hattie Zhou; Mohammad Pezeshki; I. Rish; G. Dumas

record.tranche_reason: Tests epoch-wise double descent in a grokking setting using validation loss, rather than reproducing the original double-descent method and settings.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites results from other work on double descent and slingshots; these are not recorded as findings of this study. It reports its own validation-loss trajectory and sample-fraction/generalization-time results.
record.test_reason: A grokking paper whose only result on the claim is a one-sentence observation. In a 2-layer transformer on modular arithmetic, validation loss falls, rises, then falls to zero over training. That is an epoch-wise shape in a new setting (algorithmic tasks, grokking regime), not a different method aimed at the original question, so T3 rather than T2. No numbers, figure call-out or uncertainty are given for it.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The main conclusions are that early-training loss oscillations, quantified by spectral energy, predict later grokking, and that grokking is linked to loss-landscape geometry: a perturbed valley, slingshots, and ill-conditioned Hessians. The double-descent remark is a side observation in Related works that frames grokking as a very slow double descent; it is not a tested conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: Studies grokking and loss-landscape dynamics in arithmetic-task transformers; it does not perform the original model-size or sample-size double-descent sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization time and grokking depend on training-data fraction, learning rate, and weight decay; the paper reports that larger learning rates can speed grokking up to a weight-decay-dependent threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: On the log-Rosenbrock function, some optimizers show a double descent in distance to the global minimum when landing in the ravine.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimization error (distance to optimum) on synthetic test functions can follow a fall-rise-fall curve over iterations. This concerns optimization, not generalization error.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitted generalization step t4 decreases with training fraction as a power law; intrinsic dimension co-varies with performance oscillations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More training data shortens time to grokking; layer intrinsic dimension tracks oscillations during grokking.

record.problems: The authors caution that loss-surface visualizations use a dramatic dimensionality reduction. The explicit double-descent statement concerns validation loss and does not provide numeric values or uncertainty for that trajectory.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep; a single architecture (~4e5 parameters).
No quantified test-error-over-epochs curve, no variation in model size or label noise, and no comparison of where the peak falls.
Data fraction is varied only for time to grokking; test error versus sample size is not measured.
No non-deep model classes and no interpolation-threshold comparison.
Intrinsic dimension is not used to predict peak location.
No label noise. Weight decay is swept, but only final accuracy is reported, not peak height.

missing.what: Validation accuracy trajectories for modular addition across data sizes, showing a plateau and then grokking with no rise in error. Bears on whether the epoch-wise shape holds for error rather than loss.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is this study. The V2 evidence is a single unquantified sentence, so weight it lightly. Grokking may be a distinct phenomenon in which loss shows a bump while accuracy plateaus. Tranche changed from the reader's T2 to T3.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error measurement across model sizes.
Reports validation loss in a grokking setting, not a systematic test-error sweep over training time across model classes.
Varies training-data fraction and reports generalization time, not whether test error rises as sample size increases near interpolation.
No general comparison of model classes across interpolation thresholds.
Measures intrinsic dimension and its association with training behavior, but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and samples.
Does not test label-noise-driven peaks, multiple descent peaks, or disappearance of peaks under optimally tuned regularization.
Does not re-count complexity by an effective number of parameters or test whether that converts a second descent into a U-shaped curve.

relationships.condition: Validation accuracy (error) over training, same setting
relationships.reason: From the text (Fig. 24 caption), not a row: validation accuracy stays flat, at 0 or at the training fraction, then grows. The error curve therefore plateaus rather than rising, so the fall-rise-fall shape appears in loss but not in accuracy-based error.
relationships.display_finding: Validation accuracy remained flat at zero or the training fraction before increasing, so accuracy-based error lacked the intermediate rise observed in loss.
